title: Multiparadigm Benchmark of Molecular Docking: From Physics to Co-Folding and Hybrid Models.
authors: Xu, Ao; Lam, Jordy Homing; Nakano, Aiichiro; Katritch, Vsevolod
journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
one_liner_zh: 该文系统比较了物理、混合重打分和共折叠对接方法在蛋白质-配体对接中的泛化能力，揭示了AI共折叠方法在新型靶标上的记忆化缺陷，并强调物理采样与AI方法的互补性，对蛋白质结构计算中的对接方法选择与集成有重要参考价值。
abstract: Generalizability of molecular docking predictions across novel protein targets and distinct small-molecule chemotypes is key to the successful application of deep learning co-folding approaches in drug discovery, as highlighted by recent benchmarks, including Runs-n-Poses [Skrinjar, P.; et al.Nat. Struct. Mol. Biol.2026, 33, 782-794.]. To compare generalizability across physics-based, hybrid rescoring models, and co-folding approaches, we systematically benchmarked several molecular docking tools representing these paradigms. Our results support previous observations that co-folding approaches show superior performance on targets resembling their training datasets. However, they deteriorate sharply to unacceptably low 20-40% success rates on novel dissimilar systems, consistent with memorization. In contrast, physics-based and hybrid methods exhibit greater out-of-distribution robustness, maintaining more than 60% success rates for docking protein-ligand complexes with minimal similarity to previously known complexes. Our results highlight the complementarity of AI-based approaches and methods based on physical sampling in all-atom models, in terms of their applicability range, and argue for the benefits of tighter integration.
abstract_zh: 分子对接预测在新颖蛋白质靶标和不同小分子化学类型上的泛化能力，是深度学习共折叠方法在药物发现中成功应用的关键，正如最近的基准测试（包括Runs-n-Poses [Skrinjar, P.; et al. Nat. Struct. Mol. Biol. 2026, 33, 782-794.]）所强调的那样。为了比较基于物理的方法、混合重打分模型和共折叠方法之间的泛化能力，我们系统性地基准测试了代表这些范式的几种分子对接工具。我们的结果支持先前的观察，即共折叠方法在与训练数据集相似的靶标上表现出优越的性能。然而，在新颖且不相似的系统上，它们的性能急剧下降至不可接受的20-40%成功率，这与记忆化现象一致。相比之下，基于物理的方法和混合方法在分布外鲁棒性方面表现更佳，在对接与已知复合物相似性极低的蛋白质-配体复合物时，保持了超过60%的成功率。我们的结果突显了基于人工智能的方法与基于全原子模型中物理采样的方法在适用范围上的互补性，并论证了更紧密整合的益处。
